by which I have been as if deluded before me and have fallen into confusion in an instant."
"I have fallen from my realm due to the exhaustion of my own merit, and my life is spent;
driven away, I am quickly going to my destruction before I can even reach my own abode.
Though he desired to go to his own abode, he was unable to go there either.
Terrified to an even greater degree, he wept,
and this thought arose in him:
"I am utterly deprived of my supernatural power."
"May I not fall under the power of the ascetic Gautama; may my life not come to an end in the presence of this enemy. What if I were to vanish from here and pass away outside the Buddha-field?"
Just as not even a single being in my Buddha-field could see him when he was passing away,
yet he was unable to vanish or flee to the cardinal or intermediate directions;
there, right where he was, he saw himself bound at the neck with fivefold bonds.
Becoming even more enraged and terrified, he wept aloud and spoke thus:
"Alas! My dear son and kinsmen, shall I never see you again?"
Then a Māra named Ghoṣavati, having assumed the form of a seated universal monarch, spoke thus to the Evil Māra:
"O sir, why do you weep today with a sorrowful mind, your voice and face full of lamentation?"
Quickly go for refuge to the best in all the world, the fearless and supreme sage, the protector;
he is the shelter, the resort, the lamp, and the lord who removes the three sufferings of the world. By attending upon him, you will surely attain peace and happiness.

"Homage to that supreme person, the liberator from old age, sickness, and death!
I go for refuge to that Buddha, the Blessed One. And he spoke further as follows:
O Protector, from this great and most perilous fear, may I be swiftly released from the bonds of the sage.

who was blinded by delusion and provoked against you— have offered a loud confession of my transgression.
"I confess all that before you, having established you as my witness.
And when Māra the Evil One had gone for refuge to the Buddha, the Blessed One, with words of satisfaction, he then perceived himself as liberated.
But when this thought occurred to him again:
Thinking, "I shall depart from this assembly," he again perceived himself as bound at the neck with fivefold bonds.
When he was no longer able to go anywhere, he then generated a mind seeking protection and refuge in the presence of the Blessed One.
He perceived himself as being released once more, and he perceived himself as being bound and released up to seven times while remaining seated right there.
The third chapter, "The Subduing of Māra," from the *Mahāsannipāta-ratnaketu-sūtra*, is completed.

Those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who will appear in the future in the ten directions, in various world-systems, they too shall speak this dhāraṇī, seal, and analysis of words called "The Destroyer of the Aggregate of the Heart of the Dharma of Dependent Origination through the Equality of Vajra-Dharma"; they shall empower it and mutually rejoice in it.
Then, indeed, those bodhisattvas mahāsattvas in those buddha-fields questioned their respective Blessed Ones:

"Blessed One, what is this dhāraṇī-seal, the analysis of the words for entering the prophecy, which effects the destruction of the accumulation of the heart of the dharma of dependent origination— the equality of vajra-dharma— which we have never heard before,
and which possesses such manifold qualities?"
Thus endowed with inconceivable qualities of dharma, it brings unobstructed light to all phenomena and leads even to their pacification.

May the Blessed One teach that dhāraṇī, which destroys the accumulation of the heart of the dependent nature through the equality of vajra-dharma; which provides the prophecy for entering the distinctions of words, seals, and phrases; and which crushes the power and domain of all Māras, and so forth.
It leads to final nirvana in the realm of nirvana without remainder, for the benefit of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world,
and for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the great multitude of gods and humans.
Then those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, said this to those bodhisattvas:
"Noble sons, we too shall go to that Sahā world-system where that Tathāgata Śākyamuni dwells, the Arhat, the perfectly enlightened Buddha.
And those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who currently reside, stay, and maintain themselves in various other directions throughout the ten quarters..."

In all those world-systems, they— all surrounded by hosts of bodhisattvas and preceded by the community of śrāvakas— will go to this Sahā world-system where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One, dwells;
and together with that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, [they will hear] this [dhāraṇī] which shatters the elevation of the heart of dependent origination through the equality of Vajradharma.
They shall speak the prophecy for entering the distinctions of the words of the *dhāraṇī-mudrā*, and they shall empower one another and rejoice together for the benefit of all sentient beings,

for the prevention of deeds of misconduct, for the fulfillment of the *Bhadracaryā*, and for the perfection of unsurpassed knowledge. All those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, having assembled today in this Sahā world-system, are surrounded by a host of bodhisattvas.

Preceded by the community of disciples, they will proclaim this *dhāraṇī*, which is the seal of the analysis of the words and entry into the *mudrā* of the *dhāraṇī* that destroys the accumulation of the heart of phenomena based on the equality of Vajradharma.
Therefore, whoever among you desires that [dhāraṇī] which destroys the accumulation of the heart of phenomena based on the equality of Vajradharma—

To hear the prophecy concerning the entry into the distinctions of the words of the *dhāraṇī-mudrā*; to worship those immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, Blessed Ones, who reside in a single Buddha-field for a single eon—numbering as many as the sands of the river Ganges; to hear their teachings;
and [to behold] all the arrays of the ornaments of the Buddha-fields within the domain of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, gods, and Māras.

And in order to see those many Buddhas who have assembled— beings never before seen or heard of— let him now go together with us to that Sahā world-system where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, dwells.
Then those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas said this to those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones:

"So be it, Venerable Blessed One; we shall go together with the Tathāgata to that Sahā world-system where that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, resides—to hear that [teaching] which has never been heard before, the *Vajradharmasamatāpratītyadharmahṛdayasamucchrayavidhvaṃsanī*."
In order to hear the prophecy concerning the entry into the distinctions of the words of the dhāraṇīs and mudrās,

we shall, at one time and on one occasion, in a single buddha-field, honor immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, Blessed Ones, as they remain, live, and maintain themselves; and from them, we shall also hear the Dharma.
And there we shall behold that Sahā world-system adorned with the four arrays of the domain of supernormal powers;
and we shall behold those arrays of the great assemblies.
If, while that dhāraṇī is being recited in that buddha-field, we obtain a place [to hear it].

And we shall be able to pay homage to those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, to attend upon them, to worship them, to hear their Dharma, and likewise to see those Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas, as they have assembled there.
Then those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in each of their respective Buddha-fields, spoke thus to their own Bodhisattvas, Mahāsattvas, and great Śrāvakas:
"O sons of good family, do not harbor such doubts, nor should you entertain such skepticism regarding the possibility of entry and space within this world-system.
For what reason? Because—"
Infinite is the ripening of sentient beings through the skillful knowledge of the equality of entering the domain of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
O sons of good family, that Tathāgata Śākyamuni possesses vast scope and is endowed with great skill in means.
O sons of good family, whatever sentient beings there may be who are comprised within the realm of sentient beings and dependent upon the elements and sense-bases—

If, for the sake of argument, each one of those beings were to have a physical body as large as Mount Sumeru, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni would be able to cause all those beings with such bodies to enter into a single mustard seed.
Furthermore, each individual being would have a vast field and space, yet they would not come within the range of sight of one another.
Furthermore, not even a single mustard seed would be perceived as either diminished or filled by the entry of the great bodies of all sentient beings;
such, noble sons, was the skill in means possessed by that Tathāgata Śākyamuni.
Furthermore, noble sons, whatever constitutes hardness, all that is the earth element.
That Tathāgata Śākyamuni is able to cause that entire earth element to enter into the tip of a single atom;
yet, by the entry of the entire earth element into that single atom-tip, no deficiency or fullness would be perceived in it.
The Tathāgata Śākyamuni is endowed with such skill in means.
Furthermore, noble sons, whatever moisture is perceived, all that is the water element (*abdhātu*).
That Tathāgata Śākyamuni is able to cause that entire water element to enter into the tip of a single hair;
yet, by the entry of the entire water element into that single tip of a hair, no decrease or increase would be perceived in it.
Furthermore, noble sons, whatever wind-element is known that is capable [of movement], the Tathāgata Śākyamuni is able to cast all that wind-element into a single pore of his skin.
And although the entire wind-element has been introduced into that single pore, it moves within it with ample space, as if in its own domain.
Furthermore, sons of good family, whatever heat is perceived, all that is the fire element (*tejodhātu*).
It has gone...
[into] that atom of dust (*paramāṇurajas*), and that entire fire element moves within it with ample space, as if in its own domain.

Furthermore, noble sons, Śākyamuni the Tathāgata is able to place all the Buddha-fields in the ten directions, together with all those sentient beings and those four great elements, within the tip of a single atom. And within that infinitesimal atom, all those sentient beings— along with those great elements and moving about their respective spheres of activity— could move about with ample space.
And there would be no mutual interference among them, nor would the diminution or increase of even a single speck of dust therein be perceived.
Endowed with such skillful means (upāyakauśalya) is that Tathāgata Śākyamuni.

Furthermore, sons of good family, as many as are the activities of the six sense bases, the grasping, the vows, the empowerments, the paths of speech, the sounds, the syllables, the utterances, the three types of formative forces, the ends of actions, the investigations into the aggregates, the accumulations, and the various modes of conduct belonging to all sentient beings throughout the three times—

And whatever [is encompassed by] all... having transcended it, and however many enjoyments and usages belonging to all sentient beings throughout the three times there may be that are experienced as pleasure and pain—all those the Tathāgata Śākyamuni knows in a single moment.
By means of such knowledge of the miraculous manifestation of marks, he [knows them].
The Tathāgata Śākyamuni is without conceptualization, free from discursive thought, and effortless; he is the one who has fully realized the three limits of time.

Sons of good family, it is by means of such immeasurable skill in the wisdom that enters the domain of the Buddhas, and through his equanimity and the skillful means for maturing sentient beings, that the Tathāgata Śākyamuni is endowed with these qualities.

Furthermore, in this [assembly], there were indeed immeasurable and incalculable hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas present in each of the Tathāgatas’ various assemblies, who had reached the further shore of knowledge regarding the domain of vows and supernatural powers.
The fifth chapter, the Chapter on Characteristics, from the *Ratnaketu-parivarta*, a Mahāyāna sūtra of the Great Assemblage, is completed.
(Kurumiya 121) VI. Now at that time, from the eastern direction, the Tathāgata named Akṣobhya,
together with immeasurable and incalculable Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, by the power of the empowerment of the miraculous transformations of the Buddha-realm, [arrived].
Having set out, he reached this buddha-field in a mere instant, arriving at the central four-continent world system where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One,
resides; and having arrived, he stood upon a lotus seat that appeared spontaneously.
Those bodhisattva mahāsattvas also stood upon lotus seats that had appeared through their own supernatural power.
With these as their leaders, immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, Blessed Ones— equal in number to the atoms of dust in Buddha-fields—
remaining, dwelling, and maintaining themselves, in that very instant, moment, and second, [reached] this Buddha-field, the central four-continent world-system.

Having arrived at that world-system, each Tathāgata, together with immeasurable and incalculable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and hundreds of thousands of nayutas of koṭis of śrāvakas, proceeded to where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni— the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha— was dwelling.
And as they arrived one after another, they sat down upon lotus thrones that appeared spontaneously.
Furthermore, at that time, from the southern direction, the Tathāgata named Ratnadhvaja arrived and, proceeding in detail, sat down upon a lotus filament.
Likewise from the northern direction... (Kurumiya 122)
The Tathāgata named Dundubhisvara came and sat upon the filaments of a lotus.
Furthermore, at that time, the Tathāgata named Amitāyus came from the western direction and sat upon the filaments of a lotus;
likewise, the Tathāgata named Vairocana came from below and sat upon the filaments of a lotus.

From the northeastern direction, the Tathāgata named Jñānaraśmirāja, together with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of bodhisattva mahāsattvas— equal in number to the atoms within immeasurable and incalculable Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the river Ganges— set forth from there by means of the empowerment of the miraculous manifestations of the Buddha-realm and,
in a single moment of thought, arrived at this Buddha-field, at the central four-continent world-system.
Having arrived at the world-system where the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Perfectly Awakened One,
was dwelling, he sat down upon a lotus lion-throne that had appeared spontaneously.
Those bodhisattva mahāsattvas also sat down upon lotus seats, each created through the empowerment of the power of their respective merits.
And those bodhisattvas assembled from the ten directions—some rained down a shower of Jāmbūnada gold as an act of worship for the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones;
some circumambulated the entire buddha-field;
some, thirsting to hear the Dharma, stood before the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, with palms joined in reverence; and some... [prostrated themselves].

Then, at that time, Subhūti, acting as a youth, with palms joined together, filled this entire buddha-field without exception with song through the power of his own supernatural faculties and the empowerment of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and spoke thus: (Kurumiya 123)
The moon-like sages, who sever all doubts, have assembled;
this perfection of the Saṅgha, never before seen or heard, is now clearly visible.
This field has become a true shrine, honored by all fields.
Today the Fully Awakened Ones, the suns among sages, have arrived for no reason other than this:
[to bring about] the five corruptions... today is the casting down of the Māras and the dark faction.
"For this purpose indeed have you gathered here: that there may be a compendium of virtuous practices. Listen to the peaceful nature of reality (dharmatā);
having done so, you shall indeed become perfectly awakened ones."
Armed with the armor of patience, you shall understand the Mahāyāna practice of the path;
for the sake of exhausting all afflictions, you shall today hear this dhāraṇī. [You shall hear] those [teachings] that [bring about] the destruction of all [afflictions].
"Seated upon their thrones, let them indeed teach this protection:
the *Aparājitā* dhāraṇī, the compendium of all dharmas.
Then, at that very moment, immeasurable and incalculable Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who had attained patience spoke with one voice as follows:

May the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, sit upon these lotus-thrones; may they today teach, O Greatly Compassionate Ones, the discourse that is cultivated by supreme great loving-kindness and patience, refined as the outflow of fearlessness, which encompasses all dharmas, which causes [fear]... which brings down the banner of Māra, raises high the banner of Dharma, and crushes all afflictions.

It subdues all enemies, cuts through all doubts, and is the unsurpassed protection for all bodhisattvas; it reveals the knowledge and vision of all dharmas, mindfulness, intelligence, progress, and steadfastness, as well as the skillful means and wisdom of all conduct; it is the samādhi and dhāraṇī that establishes the basis for the perfection of all happiness, and it leads one into the skillful knowledge of the light of entering into patience.

...up to the heart-dhāraṇī of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment— for the sake of fame and happiness, for dwelling in comfort, for the increase of eloquence and mindfulness, for the non-forgetting of what has been heard and its retention, ... for the upholding of the training, for being a vessel of mindfulness, for the accomplishment of conduct, and for the attainment of awakening.

May the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, now teach this *dhāraṇī* here for us, so that the guidance of the Dharma may endure for a long time through their grace, so that the lineage of the Three Jewels may not perish, so that the entire path to unsurpassed awakening may be revealed, so that there may be no differentiation between the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), space, and suchness;

so that there may be no differentiation between self, sentient being, life-force, nourishment, or person; and so that there may be no differentiation from the limit of reality, which is characterized by the sameness of all phenomena as being unborn, unarisen, unceasing, and non-existent.
For the sake of the non-differentiation of the elements of earth, water, fire, wind, space, and consciousness,

may all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, here recite for us the *dhāraṇīs* composed within the maṇḍala of the method of all phenomena, so that upon hearing them, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of beings may become witnesses to the Three Jewels.
And may beings act as spiritual friends and benefactors to one another;
and may immeasurable and incalculable beings resolve their minds upon unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, become irreversible, and receive prophecies.
And may all those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, remain established in silence for the sake of teaching the Dharma upon those filaments of lotuses.

And they entered that samādhi called "Entering the Equality of Aspiration toward the Domain of the Buddhas," such that by the mere sight of the Blessed Buddhas contained within all Buddha-fields, the mental afflictions (*kleśas*) and the mental factors (*citta-caittas*) of those [beings] contained within this Buddha-field were pacified.
And each single being perceives thus:
"The Tathāgata alone has attended to me with his entire mind and taught the Dharma that pacifies all fevers..."
Then, at that time, all the sentient beings included within this entire buddha-field, their faculties fully restored, joined their palms and spoke with one voice:
"May the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, teach us the Dharma!"
May the venerable ones teach us the Dharma, O Sugata;
may we practice with application toward the teachings of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.

Then, at that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, for the purpose of making an offering to other Buddhas, Blessed Ones, empowered this entire Buddha-field with a sublime, most excellent, and distinguished fragrance that transcended all arrays of perfumes;
and he [empowered] all sentient beings within all Buddha-fields with various jewel-flowers, garlands, ointments, and various ornaments of parasols, banners, and flags.
Having empowered his hands with fullness for the purpose of making offerings to the remaining Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, he spoke thus:
"May the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, whoever they may be, who are currently present throughout the ten directions, attend to me."

By virtue of my previous vow, I have thus awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment in this most degraded world of the five corruptions, for those whose intentions are ruined, who have lost their way, who are cast into the darkness of ignorance and the gloom of the cataracts of affliction, who are headed toward the three lower realms, who are beset by unwholesome states, who are devoid of all that is wholesome, who are shunned by all the wise, and who commit the acts of immediate retribution.
Out of compassion for those beings who reject the true Dharma, revile the noble ones, and possess hearts devoid of mercy, and through the exertion of the power of great compassionate vigor,
in order to pacify cold, heat, wind, and sun,
I travel on foot to villages, towns, market towns, districts, and royal capitals.

For the sake of the welfare of sentient beings, I consume food that is meager, coarse, tasteless, utterly loathsome, and disagreeable. ... I wear robes made of cotton scraps or rags from dust heaps. I make use of lodgings and seats in mountains, peaks, caves, forests, and groves.

Armed with the armor of skillful means, great compassion, and vigor, I speak various kinds of discourse for the sake of sentient beings: I speak of royal sovereignty for the kṣatriyas; I speak of the Vedas and the stars for the brahmins.

To his ministers, he spoke of the affairs of the realm and its administrative offices; to physicians, of the elements, medicinal herbs, and their applications; to merchants, of buying and selling; to householders, of devotion to their occupations; and to women, of complexion, ornaments, sons, prosperity, and the absence of rivals.
To the śramaṇas, I speak discourses devoted to the three types of action characterized by patience and gentleness;
for the sake of maturing sentient beings, I urge them toward the attainment of what has not yet been attained and the realization of what has not yet been realized.
For the sake of realizing that which has not yet been realized,
for the liberation of those who are not liberated, I endure various kinds of sufferings;
I wander through the countryside to bring sentient beings to maturity.
Moreover, these beings there revile and abuse me... they falsely accuse me with untruthful words;
they accuse me with hypocrisy, flattery, deceit, guile, lying, harsh speech, and feminine words;
they throw dust upon me.
They exert their prowess for my destruction with showers of weapons, poison, fire, discuses, tomara-spears, arrows, swords, śakti-lances, axes, clubs, and stones;
they release elephants, venomous serpents, lions, tigers, bulls, buffaloes, boars, and great wrestlers to kill me;
and they fill my dwellings, monasteries, and gabled halls with impurity and foul odors.
And when my disciples had entered within the city, these ignoble beings, engaged in improper conduct such as dancing and singing,
exerted themselves by means of many hundreds of thousands of stratagems to kill me.

They are intent upon the disappearance of the teaching, the extinguishing of the lamp of the guidance of the Dharma, the felling of the banner of the Dharma, the breaking apart of the ship of the Dharma, and the scattering of my Dharma-sacrifice.

Indeed, at this very time, all the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, survey the guidance of the Dharma of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones— just as those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, having convened a great assembly in this defiled Buddha-field of the five corruptions,

did so for the sake of the long endurance of the guidance of the True Dharma, for the sake of crushing the power and domain of all Māras, and for the sake of the non-interruption and maintenance of the lineage of the Three Jewels.

For the purpose of increasing the roots of virtue in sentient beings; for the purpose of subduing all enemies and adversaries through the Dharma; for the purpose of pacifying for sentient beings the strife, quarrels, famine, disease, foreign armies, imprisonment, conflict, disputes, untimely cold, heat, wind, rain, faults of body, speech, and mind, and wrong views;
for the purpose of winning over all gods, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, and non-humans; and for the purpose of protecting all houses, villages, towns, and kingdoms.

For the purpose of destroying all deceit, poisons, *kākhorda* spells, delusions, bad dreams, and evil omens; for the purpose of providing all grains, medicinal herbs, fruits, flowers, and essences for the sustenance of sentient beings; for the purpose of enjoining the Kṣatriyas, Brāhmaṇas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras to virtuous conduct;

for the purpose of generating the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*) and leading them into the perfections (*pāramitā*); and for the purpose of increasing the skill in means and wisdom, mindfulness, intelligence, comprehension, courage, and eloquence of the Bodhisattvas, the Mahāsattvas.

For the sake of attaining mastery in the knowledge of the consecration, the stages, the consolations, and the entry [into the path], this Dharma discourse— the prophecy concerning the entry into the distinctions of the words of the seal and the dhāraṇī that shatters the elevation of the heart of the dependent nature through the equality of Vajradharma— was spoken, empowered, and mutually rejoiced in by those previous Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas.

It is well; even now, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, who currently reside, dwell, and maintain themselves in the ten directions, having come together, assembled, and gathered here in my buddha-field during this age of five corruptions— all of them, for the protection of this buddha-field, [expound] this *Vajradharmasamatāpratītyadharmahṛdayasamucchrayavidhvaṃsanīdhāraṇīmudrāpadaprabhedapraveśavyākaraṇa*.

"Speak this Dharma-discourse; empower one another; rejoice in what has been spoken by each other, so that the guidance of the True Dharma may endure for a long time, for the sake of crushing the power and domain of all Māras, as previously described in detail, up to the attainment of the shore of unobstructed knowledge, out of compassion, at my request, so that the guidance of the True Dharma may remain for a long time in this Buddha-field and not be transgressed."
"It shall be of a nature that cannot be subverted by any heterodox teachers.
Furthermore, for the sake of ensuring that the lineage of the Three Jewels is not interrupted, the essence of the Dharma shall be the sustenance for all sentient beings.
Then those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, spoke thus:
Thus it is; we must certainly perform the work of a Buddha.

In this buddha-field, we shall sustain the guidance of the Dharma for its long endurance, for the purpose of crushing the power of the domain of all Māras, and until reaching the further shore of unobstructed knowledge—namely, this prophecy concerning the entry into the distinctions of the words of the seal and the dhāraṇī that shatters the accumulation of the heart of the dependent nature of the equality of Vajradharma.
"We shall speak this Dharma-discourse.
Let all sentient beings whatsoever who are included within this Buddha-field listen! Namely: Aṅkara, aṅkara!"
Bhaṅkara, Prabhaṅkara!
Fear not here;
you are my friend.

Inexpressible by the path of speech, the entrance into the great accumulation of merit, sealed with great compassion—may the eye of Dharma, which is the correct practice for all, blaze for a long time! May all the bulls among sages, empowered by the power of attaining the samādhi and wisdom of great compassion, and by the power of loving-kindness, renunciation, and supreme vigor, remain for the benefit and increase of all beings. Svāhā!
Then, at that very moment, all sentient beings included within all buddha-fields spoke thus three times:
"Homage to all buddhas!
Homage, homage to all buddhas!"
And they spoke thus: "Oh, what a great wonder is this assembly of sages!
Oh, what a great wonder is this gathering of bodhisattva mahāsattvas and great śrāvakas!"

Sentient beings established in wholesome qualities, who have extracted the essence from their assemblies and are purified in three respects, will cross over the conduct of awakening.
They will attain the *ratnadhvaja* (Jewel Banner) samādhi, by which samādhi they will become skilled in the knowledge of discernment regarding all samādhis.

And at the time of death, those sentient beings will see before them immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, Blessed Ones, surrounded by hosts of monks and preceded by hosts of bodhisattvas, staying and maintaining their lives.
They will see those [Buddhas] teaching the Dharma,
and from the presence of those Blessed Buddhas, they will hear the Dharma being taught, endowed with such meanings, phrases, and syllables,
that having attained the most distinguished, noble, and spiritual joy and gladness, all their karmic obstructions and unwholesome [deeds] [will be purified].
They shall cease together with their constituent dharmas at the moment of final consciousness.
And by virtue of all their aspirations, they shall be born through miraculous birth in completely pure Buddha-fields,
in those Buddha-fields where the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, currently reside and maintain themselves, proclaiming the pure discourse of the Mahāyāna.
In those buddha-fields, those beings will dwell together with those who have set out in the Mahāyāna, who are endowed with unobstructed knowledge, and whose minds are equal to space;
and before long, they themselves will become endowed with those very qualities.
Furthermore, those beings will not be reborn again in a defiled Buddha-field of the five corruptions; rather, through their own vows, they will swiftly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

Sustained by these ten qualities, those beings—whether now or in the future—who shall kindle this guide of the True Dharma and this Dharma-discourse of the *dhāraṇī-mudrā*, will be sustained by the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
They will take it up, and even having committed it to writing, they will preserve it;
those bodhisattva mahāsattvas, empowered by all the buddhas and bodhisattvas, shall become completely liberated from all secondary afflictions.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, addressed Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors: "O worthy ones, whatever Buddhas, Blessed Ones, have gathered here from the ten directions— all of you, for the sake of compassion,
for the purpose of purifying external phenomena in this world-system, for the ripening of sentient beings, and for the demonstration of the conduct of awakening."
For the defeat of Māra’s faction; for the raising of the banner of Dharma; for the manifestation of all the works of a Buddha; for the non-interruption of the lineage of the Three Jewels;

for the pacification of all diseases; for the warding off of all malevolent beings; for protection from all fears; for the abandonment of all wrong views; for the entry upon the path to enlightenment and the fulfillment of the ten powers of a Tathāgata; and for the exhaustion of all karma and afflictions—such is this marvelous and extraordinary [teaching].

"A Dharma discourse entitled 'The Prophecy of Entry into the Profound Dhāraṇī-Phrases' has been previously heard being spoken, by which there is protection for houses, villages, towns, cities, and provinces, up to protection for the four continents; protection for gods, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, and non-humans; protection for grains, medicinal herbs, leaves, flowers, fruits, and crops;
and protection for Dharma-preachers and listeners of the Dharma, for the sake of attaining the unimpeded dhāraṇī and for entering into knowledge equal to space."
For the sake of attaining the omniscient wisdom of the single principle,

O friends, in this Dharma-discourse, each and every phenomenon in this Buddha-field has been empowered by these Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, in ten ways through the outflows of the wisdom that enters into great compassion.
Friends, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have fully enjoyed this Buddha-field for the sake of establishing all wholesome dharmas.

For all those born in any Buddha-field, this Buddha-field has become a shrine, occupying the place of a teacher, esteemed as the Master, and worthy of veneration— even for those who have committed the five acts of immediate retribution and are possessed of unwholesome dharmas.
That karmic obstruction, with its undesirable fruit, goes to complete exhaustion without remainder.
And all those, having abandoned their karmic obstructions, become established in wholesome dharmas.
This, friends, is the great heroic deed of the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones.
In this buddha-field, friends, you must respectfully take up and protect this Dharma;
and those individuals, whether householders or renunciants, who uphold the true Dharma and practice it according to the teaching, must be protected.
In this way, it will lead to your welfare and happiness.
(Kurumiya 176) Then, at that time, the Tathāgata Kusumadhvaja, in order to describe the qualities and benefits of this Dharma discourse, spoke thus:
"Having filled all buddha-fields with gold, one would protect [them]."
Whoever should apply this very [text] for the sake of worshipping the Leaders,
and whoever should uphold this supreme primary sūtra—
that wise one shall obtain immeasurable merit in this way.
Then indeed, the Tathāgata Ratnacchatraśrī also spoke thus:
"By giving gold coins as numerous as the sands of the river Gaṅgā to the bulls among sages, one obtains merit exactly as one does by dedicating this sūtra."

Then indeed, the Tathāgata Girikūṭa also spoke thus: "Suppose someone, with a joyful and serene mind, were to offer to the Buddhas for the sake of worship a mass of clouds consisting of a multitude of parasols made of heaps of excellent flowers, covering the very sky."
Even if one were to uphold this sūtra at a later time, during the terrifying and turbulent period when [the Dharma] has declined,
not even all sentient beings together would be able to describe the measure of this merit. Then, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, spoke thus:

O Sage, whoever here desires merit or seeks the thinning of hindrances— whether it be one person or another— should with devotion light a lamp before you, O Muni, and hold a wick the size of Mount Meru, soaked in scented oil, with a radiant countenance for ten million eons.
In times when the [teachings] have declined, one should proclaim this sūtra in the assembly; the merit from this is superior.
Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya also spoke thus:
"The wise one who would cultivate patience and always exert vigor,"
Constantly devoted to meditation, with a body composed in concentration, one should expand wisdom;
for he who, in this degenerate age (*kaliyuga*), maintains this seal of the True Dharma.
"This is patience, this is peerless vigor, and his wisdom is incomparable.
Then, indeed, the Tathāgata Virajabalavikrāmī also spoke thus:
"Having revealed, upheld, and written down this sūtra here,"
Having caused others to grasp [the teaching] through reasoning and having caused them to recite it constantly,
and then having honored it with incense, flowers, garlands, and the finest robes—
whatever merit one thereby attains cannot be fully described.
Thus it is said.

Then indeed, those immeasurable and incalculable Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, having proclaimed the immeasurable praise, qualities, and benefits of this sutra, summoned Śakra, Brahmā, and the World-Protectors, and spoke to them thus:

"Friends, you should take up this Dharma discourse, which brings about the destruction of all karmic obstructions and afflictions; for in the future time, by the mere hearing of it, the destruction of all karmic obstructions and afflictions will occur for sentient beings."
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
And the entire assembly, including the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, with joyful minds, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
The thirteenth chapter, the Chapter on the Attainment of the Culmination of Ratnaketu, from the Mahāsannipāta Mahāyāna Sūtra, is completed.
(Kurumiya 178) [Colophon] Having edited the *Ratnaketu*, which is the foremost among dhāraṇīs that remove abundant fears, by me—
Whatever merit has been produced by one with a joyful mind and devoted with all his devotion—
by that, may this entire world immediately attain this very *Ratnaketu*, which is adorned with the teachings of the Sage’s words, clear in meaning, and exceedingly pure in its virtues.

The Compendium of the True Dharma [was composed] by the illustrious Paṭola Śāhi Vikramādityananda, together with his illustrious chief queen Surendramālā, as well as with the illustrious chief queen Uvakhī Dilnitapuṇyā.
Likewise, this great donor, Etalaga, son of Nikṣiṇa, has had this written in a book together with his wife Āśṇāti of Kasumovaḷtā, and together with his mother Aspinaśūlā.
